subject.title: Update 2026.3.24 silently drops config when HOME changes

question: When the updater HOME differs from the installed gateway service HOME and no explicit `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` is present, should OpenClaw preserve the service HOME, block until explicit migration, or add a guarded doctor migration?
rationale: The repair crosses credential-bearing config, service identity, and Unix-user boundaries, and preserving old service env blindly can conflict with stale-env hardening.

options.title: Block and require explicit migration
options.body: Detect the HOME/root mismatch before service rewrite and point the operator at a doctor migration that shows source and destination roots with backups.

options.title: Preserve authenticated service HOME
options.body: Carry the previous service HOME into update doctor/restart paths only when the installed service can be verified as OpenClaw-owned.

options.title: Document manual recovery only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and document the wrong-HOME update class as an operator-managed recovery path.

recommendation.title: Block and require explicit migration
recommendation.body: Detect the HOME/root mismatch before service rewrite and point the operator at a doctor migration that shows source and destination roots with backups.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent package-update restart path is closest to the policy decision and implementation boundary.
